# Bot needs to be more accurate with its navigation — Intake Brief

**Priority:** high · **Issue type:** bug · **Assignee:** Map

## Problem statement

The competent bot's aim **lead** is effectively not running for the enemies it shoots at. `engage`
aims at `interceptPoint(...)` only when its chosen target exposes `vx`/`vy`, but the snapshot only
carries velocity for entities with a physics body — in practice `Asteroid` and `LaneTraffic`
(`src/entities/Asteroid.ts:418`, `src/entities/LaneTraffic.ts:145`). Every formation, `chaser`,
`diver` and `patroller` enemy moves by scripted position updates with no `vx`/`vy`
(`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:121`), so the bot aims at the target's **current** position and the shot
arrives after the target has moved — the ship "often misses its target". Where a lead *is* solved,
the trajectory model is a constant-velocity straight line and the projectile speed used for the
time of flight is the **enemy** bullet speed (`assumedBulletSpeed` = 200 px/s), not the ship's own
350 px/s, so the lead is over-estimated by 75 %. Meanwhile the bot already owns a better motion
model for the same entities — the per-hazard velocity/curvature tracker plus the movement-class
trajectory sampler that hazard avoidance runs — so the fix is to apply the **same calculations to
aim as are used to predict movement**, and to give the aim a small, configurable error so it is
deliberately imperfect rather than accidentally wrong.

## Users

- **Player watching the attract/demo bot** (primary): expects a pilot whose shots connect with the
  enemy it is chasing, not one that keeps missing a curving target.
- **Producer tuning the bot in `GymBotTuning`** (secondary): wants the lead/aim error as live knobs
  and a reproducible, test-backed accuracy number rather than a subjective "looks better".
- **Developer** (secondary): wants one trajectory definition shared by prediction and aim so the
  two cannot drift apart.

### Example user stories

- As a **viewer of the demo**, I want the bot's shots to hit the chaser that is curving toward the
  ship, so the demo reads as competent rather than broken.
- As a **producer**, I want a configurable aim error so the bot is beatable and human-looking, and a
  live slider to trade accuracy for fallibility.
- As a **developer**, I want the aim solve to consume the same velocity and movement-class
  prediction as hazard avoidance, so I fix prediction once and both features benefit.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Aim lead uses the bot's own motion estimate, not the snapshot's.** The `engage` aim solve
  resolves its target's velocity from the bot-side tracker
  (`trackHazardVelocities` → `BotWorld.hazards[].vx/vy/curvature`, the same estimate the hazard
  predictor consumes) instead of the raw `BotEnemy.vx/vy` field. A moving formation/`chaser`/
  `diver`/`patroller` target that exposes no snapshot velocity is therefore led. When no estimate
  exists yet (cold start, stale, or an id-less fixture target) the solve reduces **exactly** to
  today's behaviour (aim at the current position).
- **AC2 — Solve inputs come from live physics.** The intercept solve takes the **player's**
  projectile speed and the **ship's live turn time**, not the bot's assumptions:
  `assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s, an enemy-bullet tell constant) is replaced as the aim
  time-of-flight input by the ship's live projectile speed (350 px/s `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED` /
  per-weapon speed, carried through the snapshot seam the way `getThrusterConfig()`/
  `getRotationConfig()` already are), and the fixed `aimLeadAlignSeconds` alignment term is
  derived from the live rotation model (`angularStopDisplacement` + rotation accel/decel) with the
  constant retained only as the no-config fallback. A unit test pins 200 → 350 and the
  turn-time derivation.
- **AC3 — Predict the trajectory the target will actually fly.** For a target with a fitted velocity
  and a known movement class, the intercept point is solved by advancing the target along the
  **sampled class trajectory** (`advanceHazardMotion`, the single definition of each class's
  motion, already used by `predictMinimumSeparation`) and re-estimating time of flight each
  iteration; `roamer`/unknown class/disabled motion model reproduces the constant-velocity solve
  bit-for-bit, and a stationary target reproduces the current-position aim bit-for-bit. Wrap-aware
  (torus) behaviour from AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15 is preserved.
- **AC4 — Configurable, self-correcting aim error.** A new live-tuned `aimErrorRad` (radians,
  default small — ≈0.02 rad — and applied only to intents flagged as **aim**, never to
  survival/evade/travel) perturbs the committed aim bearing from the governor's dedicated seeded
  aim-error RNG stream (deterministic per run seed, no draw at `0`, so `0` is byte-for-byte today's
  behaviour). It is independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation. The error is
  **adaptive, not fixed** (producer answer Q1): every confirmed hit on the engaged target multiplies
  the current error by `aimErrorDecay` (default ≈0.5, floored at 0), so a bot that keeps hitting
  zeroes in; the error is restored to `aimErrorRad` only after a **repositioning move** — the ship
  having moved `aimErrorResetDistance` px (default ≈60, torus-aware, measured from its position at
  the last hit) or having changed engagement target. All three knobs are live sliders via
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` / `GymBotTuning` and persisted in `src/data/bot-tuning.json`; the hit
  signal arrives through one shared scene seam (AC6), so the game and every gym feed it identically.
- **AC5 — Accuracy is measured, not asserted.** A deterministic headless aim-accuracy harness
  (seeded, fixed 60 Hz, a fixed seed list of at least three seeds, one scenario per movement class)
  reports shots fired / shots hit / mean miss distance for the new solve against the pre-change
  baseline, and a regression test asserts the pooled hit rate is strictly higher than the baseline
  and the mean miss distance lower, with `aimErrorRad = 0`. The measured before/after numbers are
  recorded on the work item.
- **AC6 — Single-sourced and gym-parity clean.** All behaviour lives in the shared `src/ai` code
  (plus the snapshot seam and the hit seam); `PlayScene`, `GymBotTuning` and every bot-bearing gym
  consume the same code, with no per-scene copy and no gym/game divergence introduced. The aim-hit
  signal is published from the shared `CombatScene` collision path — a hook beside the existing
  `onEnemyDestroyed` / `finaliseEnemyKill` seam (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:662`), plus the
  overridable `CombatScene.onEnemyDestroyed` precedent at line 1195 — never re-implemented per
  scene.
- **AC7 — Docs and tests.** `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` §9.8 (rotation skills / lead) and the §12 knob
  list describe the new solve, the new knob and the accuracy harness; unit tests cover the solve,
  the speed/turn inputs and the error draw, and `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts` (or a
  sibling integration test) exercises the end-to-end aim. All related documentation is updated to
  reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
  Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

The demo bot now only fires when it actually has a target inside its weapon range on its firing line, so it no longer sprays shots into empty space while it travels, collects or dodges; it stands still and shoots when a shot is on, closes the distance when the target is out of reach, and designers keep the sliders for the aim fallibility and the hold-station horizon.

## Constraints

- **Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md).** Shared behaviour stays in `src/ai/`; `PlayScene`, the shared
  `src/scenes/core/` code and every gym scene consume the same functions.
- **No physics constants in the bot layer.** Live ship values arrive through the `BotSnapshot` seam
  (the `getRotationConfig()` / `getThrusterConfig()` precedent), never hard-coded in `src/ai/`.
- **Deterministic and cheap.** No wall clock, seeded RNG only, same inputs → same output; the per-tick
  path stays allocation-free/bounded (it runs for every engage tick inside the 50-enemy perf
  envelope).
- **Telemetry schema unchanged.** Accuracy is measured in the test/harness layer; no new telemetry
  event kinds are introduced by this item.
- **Out of scope (record, do not absorb).** Re-driving the real enemy entities from
  `advanceHazardMotion` (a substantially larger predictor/entity unification); telemetry
  shots-fired/hit events; per-pod orbit-weapon lead; enemy aim accuracy (this item is the ship's
  aim).

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk — stale or cold tracked estimate.** The tracker needs two ticks of history, so the first
  engagement tick has no velocity. Mitigation: the documented exact fallback to the current-position
  aim, covered by a unit test.
- **Risk — the class model is not the entity's real movement.** `advanceHazardMotion` is the
  predictor's own definition; a class whose real entity diverges would still mis-lead. Mitigation:
  the AC5 harness measures per class so a diver/chaser regression is visible, and unifying the
  entities with the model is recorded as an explicit follow-up rather than silently absorbed.
- **Risk — over-leading a reverser.** Formation enemies drift and reverse; a long lead on an enemy
  that turns back over-leads further than no lead. Mitigation: the class sampler's bounded horizon
  and iteration count, plus the `aimLeadEnabled` off-switch, and the per-class measurement in AC5.
- **Risk — per-tick cost.** The aim solve runs on every engage tick near the 50-enemy perf envelope.
  Mitigation: reuse the existing bounded sampler (`HAZARD_MOTION_MAX_SAMPLES`) and its scratch
  buffers; no per-tick allocation.
- **Risk — a hit signal that lies.** Counting hits on *any* enemy (a stray bullet, an AOE, a ram)
  would sharpen the aim for the wrong reason. Mitigation: only a hit on the **engaged target** decays
  the error, and the repositioning reset keeps a streak from surviving a change of victim.
- **Risk — repositioning definition mismatch.** A distance-only rule could re-arm the error mid-fight
  during a slow strafe, or never re-arm it in a hugging fight. Mitigation: `aimErrorResetDistance` is
  a live knob, the target change also re-arms, and the AC5 harness reports the shot mix (led vs
  unled) so the rule is tuned on numbers.
- **Risk — scope creep into entity/predictor unification**, telemetry shot events or weapon-specific
  lead. Mitigation: all three are listed as out of scope; they become linked work items if wanted.
- **Assumption** — the turn actuator (deadband, inertia-aware hold) is correct; only the aim target
  changes. **Assumption** — 350 px/s is the representative ship projectile speed (pod weapons at
  300 px/s are accepted as within the aim error). **Resolved by the producer (Q1)** — the error is a
  dedicated `aimErrorRad` that decays on hits and re-arms on a repositioning move.

## Existing state

- Aim lead today: `engage` calls `interceptPoint` only when `best.point.vx/vy` are non-zero
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts:212`), passing `t.assumedBulletSpeed` (200 px/s) as the
  **projectile** speed and `t.aimLeadAlignSeconds` (0.25 s default, 0.35 s shipped tuning) as the
  alignment term.
- `interceptPoint` (`src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts:197`) is a pure constant-velocity
  iterated lead; wrap-aware since AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15, but it never consults a movement class.
- Shot speed: travelling player bullets use `PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED = 350`
  (`src/core/constants.ts:378`, `src/scenes/core/CombatCoreScene.ts:1114`); pod bullets use 300
  (`src/utils/weapons.ts:689`). `assumedBulletSpeed = 200`
  (`src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts:444`) is described in
  `src/ai/tuningFields.ts:126` as the *enemy*-bullet speed for fire tells — it is reused here for
  the ship's time of flight.
- Motion model that already exists and is already trusted for prediction:
  `trackHazardVelocities` (`src/ai/framework/hazardVelocity.ts:178`, velocity + curvature from a
  bounded position history), `resolveEnemyMovementClass`
  (`src/ai/framework/enemyMovementClass.ts:75`, archetype → class mirror of
  `src/data/enemy-configs.csv`) and `advanceHazardMotion`
  (`src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts:595`), consumed by `predictMinimumSeparation`. Its
  docstring states the evaluation arena advances live hostiles with the same call, so prediction and
  "actual movement" are meant to be one definition.
- Aim error that already exists: `BotInputGovernor` perturbs aim-flagged intents by
  `maxAimErrorRad × (1 − skill)` from a dedicated seeded stream
  (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), default `skill = 1` (off).
- The ship auto-fires (no aim gate on the trigger), so accuracy is entirely "is the nose where the
  target will be".
- Hit feedback does not exist: player-bullet damage is applied in
  `CombatScene.damageEnemyWithBullet` (`src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts:576`) and kills are
  finalised once in `finaliseEnemyKill` / `onEnemyDestroyed` (`:662`, `:1195`), but nothing tells the
  bot whether an aimed shot connected — `BotSnapshot.player` (`src/ai/botSnapshot.ts:76`) carries no
  hit signal, so AC4's adaptive error needs a new seam.
- Shot accuracy is not currently measured: the evaluation harness has kills and player hits but no
  shots-fired event (`docs/TELEMETRY.md` §event kinds).

## Desired change

- Resolve the engaged target's motion from the tracker (AC1) and keep the raw-snapshot path as the
  cold-start fallback.
- Carry the ship's live projectile speed and rotation config through the snapshot seam and feed the
  real values into the solve (AC2), plus the aim-hit count the governor needs for AC4.
- Add a class-aware intercept that samples `advanceHazardMotion`, converging time of flight against
  the sampled trajectory, and reduce exactly to the legacy solve when the class/estimate is
  unknown (AC3).
- Add `aimErrorRad` as a seeded, aim-only, live-tunable error that decays on confirmed hits and
  re-arms on a repositioning move (AC4), fed by a new shared aim-hit seam (AC6).
- Add the headless accuracy harness and record its before/after numbers (AC5).
- Update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and the knob documentation (AC7).

**Key Files:**

- `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts` — `engage` aim solve: consume the tracked motion and
  class, pass the live shot speed and turn time.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `interceptPoint`: add the class-sampled variant and
  the live turn-time input, preserving exact fallbacks.
- `src/ai/framework/hazardMotionModel.ts` — reuse `advanceHazardMotion` (no new trajectory code).
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — expose the engaged target's tracker estimate to the aim path
  (hazards already carry `vx`/`vy`/`curvature`/`movementClass`).
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — carry the ship's live projectile speed, rotation config (if not already
  present) and the aim-hit count through the structural source seam.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.ts` — publish the aim-hit hook beside `onEnemyDestroyed` /
  `finaliseEnemyKill` (single-sourced for the game and every gym).
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — thread the hit count (and the
  reposition state the governor derives from the snapshot) into the bot without local logic.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts`, `src/ai/tuningFields.ts`, `src/data/bot-tuning.json` —
  the new knob plus the `assumedBulletSpeed` description fix.
- `src/ai/botHumanLike.ts` — `aimErrorRad` / `aimErrorDecay` / `aimErrorResetDistance` in the
  governor tunables, the seeded draw and the hit-decay / reposition-reset state.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts`, `behaviours.test.ts`,
  `src/ai/botRotationSkills.integration.test.ts`, plus the new aim-accuracy harness — tests.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — §9.8 and the §12 knob table.

## Related work

- **Bot rotation skills (AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98)** — introduced the lead solve, the inertia-aware turn
  hold and the `skill` aim error; this item continues that work by fixing the solve's inputs.
- **Predict enemy movement (bot) (AH-0MVI4QDN90037DIN)** — built the hazard velocity tracker this
  item reuses for aim.
- **Movement-class seam for bot hazards (AH-0MWM0C6OW006G5SE)**, **Class-shaped hazard trajectory
  prediction (AH-0MWM0C9F9006HNXV)**, **Sampled prediction in steering and kiting
  (AH-0MWM0CB2Q003Y6AB)** — the class model and sampler the aim solve should share.
- **Seam-aware aim and intercept (AH-0MVT2VZR7000GS15)** — the torus solve that must be preserved.
- **Bot needs to be better at avoiding enemies (AH-0MWLUIOH9001XBJ3)** — the sibling play-testing
  item on prediction fidelity for *avoidance*; same diagnosis, different consumer.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item already satisfies these acceptance criteria.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

Questions were queued for the producer at intake time and answered in an interactive producer
reply (2026-11-21). The brief above reflects the accepted answers; the recommended option and the
producer's extra condition are recorded per entry.

- **Q1 (answered) — What should the configurable aim error be, and what should it default to?**
  - Options: (a) a new dedicated `aimErrorRad` (radians) applied to aim intents only, default small
    (≈0.02 rad), independent of the existing `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` degradation; (b) reuse
    `skill`/`maxAimErrorRad` and simply ship a default `skill < 1`; (c) declare a per-shot *hit*
    probability and deliberately throw the shot wide on a failed roll.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — a dedicated knob leaves the existing skill degradation intact for
    "make the bot worse on purpose" and gives one unambiguous number to tune; (c) would be a
    different (probability) model and much harder to make believable.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **"(a) — but once the bot hits the error should be
    reduced until they make a repositioning move."** Source: producer reply in this session.
    Research: the governor already owns a dedicated seeded aim-error stream
    (`src/ai/botHumanLike.ts:943`), so the decay/reset state lives beside it and needs no new RNG;
    shortening the error on a hit requires a hit signal the bot does not have today, so AC4 now
    carries the adaptive rule and AC6 the shared seam that feeds it. AC4 was rewritten to specify
    `aimErrorDecay` (multiplicative, floored at 0) and `aimErrorResetDistance` (the repositioning
    move), so both halves of the producer's condition are testable.
- **Q2 (answered) — What does "the same calculations for predicting movement as those used in
  actual movement" mean in scope?**
  - Options: (a) reuse the bot-side trajectory model the hazard predictor already uses (tracked
    velocity/curvature + `advanceHazardMotion`), leaving the enemy entities untouched; (b) also
    re-drive the real enemy entities from `advanceHazardMotion` so prediction and entity code are
    literally the same call site (much larger, touches every enemy and gym).
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it delivers the requested prediction fidelity in the bot layer only, with
    no entity/gym churn; (b) is the natural follow-up once (a) proves the model is faithful.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. (b) stays
    recorded as explicit out-of-scope in *Constraints* and becomes a follow-up item if wanted.
- **Q3 (answered) — How should "more accurate" be evidenced?**
  - Options: (a) a deterministic headless harness reporting shots fired / hits / mean miss distance
    per movement class, with a regression assertion against the pre-change baseline; (b) unit-level
    assertions on the solve only (no end-to-end number); (c) add telemetry shot events and compare
    recorded runs.
  - **Recommended: (a)** — it produces a number the producer can quote and needs no telemetry
    schema change; (c) is a much bigger change for the same evidence.
  - Answer (producer, interactive reply): **(a)**. Source: producer reply in this session. No
    telemetry schema change; the harness numbers are recorded on the work item as AC5's evidence.
- **Assumption (not a question): title scope.** The title says "navigation" while the seed body
  ("It often misses its target") is about aim. Researched `src/ai/framework/competent/behaviours.ts`,
  `steering.ts`, `botHumanLike.ts` and the snapshot seam (see *Existing state*); the defect found is
  target-prediction/aim accuracy, and the fix also tightens the ship's own turn-time prediction
  (which is navigation-adjacent). Treated as an aim/prediction-accuracy item.
- **Assumption: turn control is already adequate.** `aimAlignmentToleranceRad` (0.05 rad) and the
  inertia-aware turn hold from AH-0MV1DUSM2005HL98 are assumed correct; this item changes what the
  nose is aimed at, not how the nose is turned.

## Plan: decomposition into features (2026-11-21)

Decomposed into **8 vertical slices** in test-first, dependency order. Each slice carries the code,
its tests and (where it changes behaviour) the documentation its own consumers read; a consolidated
documentation slice closes parent AC7 because the aim solve, the knob table and the harness are one
narrative section (§9.8/§12) that reads badly if split.

| # | Child | Type | Covers | Depends on | Est. |
|---|-------|------|--------|-----------|------|
| 1 | Aim-accuracy harness and pre-change baseline (AH-0MWR04UJ5008H5WQ) | task | AC5 (measurement) | — | ~3h |
| 2 | Tracker-derived aim velocity (AH-0MWR04X10002VNDG) | feature | AC1 | 1 | ~2h |
| 3 | Live physics inputs in the aim solve (AH-0MWR04ZDU0005O8J) | feature | AC2 | 2 | ~2h |
| 4 | Class-sampled intercept solve (AH-0MWR051U6003BDB9) | feature | AC3 | 3 | ~3h |
| 5 | Shared aim-hit seam (AH-0MWR054VE006YSLN) | feature | AC6 | 1 | ~2h |
| 6 | Adaptive aim error knobs (AH-0MWR057Q8004PBOD) | feature | AC4 (+AC6 delivery) | 4, 5 | ~3h |
| 7 | Accuracy regression proof and recorded numbers (AH-0MWR05EZE0044Z01) | task | AC5 (proof) | 1–4, 6 | ~2h |
| 8 | Aim solve documentation and knob docs (AH-0MWR05J320041SAA) | docs | AC7 | 1–6 | ~2h |

**Why this order**

- **Measurement first.** The harness (slice 1) and its pinned pre-change baseline exist before any
  behaviour changes, so "more accurate" is a comparison against a recorded number rather than an
  opinion, and slice 7 turns it into an assertion.
- **One aim call site at a time.** Slices 2 → 3 → 4 each touch `engage`'s aim solve; doing them
  serially means each lands with an exact-fallback parity test before the next changes the same
  lines.
- **The error is last.** The adaptive aim error (slice 6) consumes the hit signal from slice 5 and
  perturbs the solve from slice 4, so it cannot land before either.
- **Docs close the loop** after the behaviour is real (slice 8), and the docs assertions are what
  stop §9.8/§12 drifting from the code.

**Between slices:** review the next slice's description against what actually landed, update it
(and this table) before starting, and keep the per-class harness numbers on this item current.

**Estimate:** the plan-stage effort/risk run over the eight slices reports **Small / Medium**
(O 8.5 h · M 14.5 h · P 22 h → **14.33 h expected**, **18.33 h recommended**, 76 % confidence) — a
refinement of the intake estimate (10.25 h / 15.25 h) that now carries real per-slice inputs. The
item stays **Small** and **Medium** risk, so no plan-approval pause was required.

**Review outcome:** all seven parent acceptance criteria are owned by exactly one slice (AC5 by two:
measurement in slice 1, proof in slice 7), the AC coverage review returns `proceed`, and no new
clarifying questions were needed — the producer's intake answers (Q1–Q3, recorded in the Appendix
above) resolve every open choice.

## Remediation (producer decision, 2026-11-22)

Manual play-test rejected the epic as a regression: the bot oscillates again and
is no more accurate, in **both the turn actuator and the forward/backward
(thrust/reverse) control**. Producer answers to the audit questions:

1. **(b)** Keep the aim solve; fix the oscillation. Treat the AC5 headless
   harness as incomplete — it does not capture live oscillation — and add an
   oscillation check.
2. The symptom is in **both** the turn actuator **and** the forward/backward
   (thrust/reverse) control.

### Remediation acceptance criteria

- **RAC1 — Turn oscillation is damped.** With the shipped defaults, an aim
  intent no longer thrashes left/right on successive commits: a deterministic
  control-loop harness over the shipped `BotInputGovernor` measures turn-input
  sign flips per second below a pinned threshold, and the result is asserted
  against a recorded pre-fix baseline. Aim precision is preserved (the aim
  deadband and on-target hold still apply).
- **RAC2 — Forward/backward oscillation is damped.** Thrust and reverse no
  longer toggle around the engagement-range boundary on successive ticks: the
  same harness measures thrust-on/thrust-off and reverse-on/reverse-off
  transitions per second below a pinned threshold, asserted against a recorded
  pre-fix baseline. A hysteresis band around `engagementRange` prevents the
  boundary thrash.
- **RAC3 — Oscillation harness.** The deterministic headless harness reports,
  per movement class and seed, turn sign flips and thrust/reverse transitions
  alongside the existing shots/hits/miss-distance numbers, so an oscillation
  regression is measurable rather than only visible in a play-test.
- **RAC4 — Gym↔game parity preserved.** All fixes live in the shared human-input
  governor / competent aim code; `PlayScene` and every bot-bearing gym consume
  the same code with no per-scene copy.
- **RAC5 — Docs and tests.** The turn/thrust oscillation damping and any new
  knob are documented in `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md`; unit and harness tests cover
  the damping; the full project test suite passes.




## Fire-discipline remediation (producer audit 2026-11-25)

**Producer rejection (manual review, 2026-11-25).** "The bot will sometimes appear to be
firing at nothing. It should be aware of the range of its weapons and should always seek to
be firing at a target or collecting minerals or powerups, or avoiding a hit from
weapons/enemies/asteroids. The ship should never be firing away from targets, unless
maneuvering for a defined purpose."

### Diagnosis

- Auto-fire is **unconditional** along the committed facing (`CombatCoreScene._autoFire`
  → `player.tryFire`). While the bot collects, evades or repositions, its nose points away
  from every target and it keeps shooting into empty space — exactly the "firing at nothing"
  the producer sees.
- The aim/hold solve judges a shot only by time-to-hit against `holdFireHorizonSeconds`; it
  never compares the target's distance with the active weapon's reach (`Player` /
  `WeaponDefinition.bulletLifetime`). The hold-station posture can therefore hold at
  `engagementRange` (140 px) with a short-reach weapon (Rapid ≈ 131 px) and fire at nothing.

### Remediation acceptance criteria

- **FAC1 — Weapon-range awareness.** The ship's effective weapon reach (px) is derived from the
  live active weapons (`PLAYER_BULLET_SPEED × bulletLifetime` for travelling shots, the
  `hitscan.length` for a beam, `aoe.projectileSpeed × bulletLifetime` for a random-detonation
  AOE) and carried through the `BotSnapshot` seam. The fire solution
  (`evaluateFireSolution` / `resolveFireSolution`) reports `inRange` and only counts a shot as
  a hit when the target is inside that reach; the hold-station posture and the hittable-target
  preference require it. A snapshot without a range keeps today's behaviour **exactly**
  (`0`/absent = no range gate), so the pinned fixtures and baselines stay byte-identical.
- **FAC2 — Never fire at nothing.** Demo-bot auto-fire is gated: a shot is only spawned when a
  live target (enemy, asteroid, boss) lies within the weapon reach **and** inside the fire line
  (perpendicular offset ≤ the target's hit radius + the bullet radius, ahead of the muzzle).
  While the bot is collecting, evading or repositioning with nothing in the line, no shot is
  fired. The gate is single-sourced (`hasFireLine` + one `CombatCoreScene.botFireAllowed`
  hook) and overridden identically by `PlayScene` and `GymBotTuning`; non-bot scenes are
  unaffected (`true` default).
- **FAC3 — Purposeful seek-to-fire.** With a target inside reach the bot keeps holding the aim
  axis and firing; outside reach the hold-station posture degrades to closing the distance
  (range-aware solution) instead of holding and firing into nothing.
- **FAC4 — Gym↔game parity.** All behaviour lives in the shared `src/ai` / `src/scenes/core`
  code; no per-scene copy and no gym/game divergence.
- **FAC5 — Measured and documented.** A deterministic headless A/B (the aim-accuracy arena,
  same seeds/classes) measures shots fired / hits / hit rate / shots-fired-at-nothing with the
  gate **off** vs **on**; the gated arm fires nothing at nothing and does not lose hit rate.
  Unit tests cover the range-aware solution, the fire-line predicate, the snapshot range seam
  and the scene gate; `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` describes the fire discipline.

### Remediation assumptions (documented, not blocking)

- "Firing away from targets" is the auto-fire trigger, which is unconditional today; gating the
  trigger is the minimal change that satisfies the producer's rule.
- A shot counts as "at a target" when the target's own hit radius intersects the shot line
  within the active weapon's reach; a small bullet-radius allowance is added so a body a bullet
  would clip counts as a valid target.
- The gate uses the **maximum** reach among the active weapons: if any active weapon can reach a
  body on the line, firing is purposeful.

# Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon entries from weapons.csv

## Goal
As a player, when I capture a hex that awards a weapon, I want that weapon to appear in my hangar so I can see it, equip it and fly it — and as a designer, when I add a row to `src/data/weapons.csv`, I want a matching hangar entry to exist automatically, so the unlock tree can never drift out of sync with the shipped weapon roster.

## Background — the defect this fixes
`src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` awards weapons by id (`grants: 'rapid'`, `'arc'`, `'broadside'`, `'dual'`, `'nova'`), but `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`) hand-authors only four weapons (`spread`, `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster`). Capturing ring 1's `hex-r1-3` (boss `iron-crusher`) therefore records `rapid` in `hangar.unlockedWeapons` — the save is correct — yet **nothing in the game can display it**:

- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts:935`) iterates the catalogue, so there is no row at all.
- `buildHangarWeaponOptions` (`:1017`) iterates `unlockedWeapons` but `findHangarEntry('rapid')` returns `null` → `continue`, so there is no loadout slot.
- `resolveActiveLoadout` → `ownedEntriesOf` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:1243`) drops catalogue-unknown ids, so it would not deploy even if equipped.

Affected grants and their sources:

| Hex(es) | Grant | State today |
|---|---|---|
| `hex-r1-3`, `hex-r2-4` | `rapid` | ownable, invisible |
| `hex-r2-1` | `arc` | ownable, invisible |
| `hex-r2-2` | `broadside` | ownable, invisible |
| `hex-r2-5` | `dual` | ownable, invisible |
| `hex-r2-12` | `nova` | ownable, invisible |
| `hex-r2-8`, `-9`, `-10` | `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up` | resolve to `kind: 'modifier'`, no catalogue entry (out of scope here — see Out of scope) |

The root cause is a missing guard, not a missing field: there is referential integrity in one direction (every catalogue `weaponId` must exist in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`, pinned by tests) but **none** in the other (every authored hex grant must have a catalogue entry). `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts:114` ("keeps a shipped weapon/upgrade hull that the catalogue does not itemise") codifies the fallback as intended, which quietly legitimised its misuse.

## Design — Option B (agreed with the producer)
```
weapons.csv + weapon-patterns.csv
        │
        ▼
  WEAPON_CATALOGUE ─────────────┐
                                │ deriveWeaponEntry(weapon)
  AUTHORED_ENTRIES ─────────────┤
  (hulls, modifiers, power-ups) │
        │                       ▼
        └──────────► HANGAR_CATALOGUE = AUTHORED_ENTRIES + derived weapon entries
```

- `name`, `description` and `weaponId` are **derived** from the CSV row — drift is structurally impossible and the CSV's own player-facing description ("Adds single bullets at a much higher fire rate.") is reused as hangar copy.
- `price` and `minRing` are **authored**, never derived. A small side table (`WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY: weapon id → { price, minRing }`) promotes a derived entry to purchasable; absence from the table means **grant-only** (`minRing: GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`, zero price) — the existing `hull-4` precedent: representable, grantable, visible once owned, never sold.
- Pricing must not be derived from shipped tuning. `src/utils/weapons.ts` already rules this out: *"Baselines are frozen history — they are never re-derived from the shipped data, or a regression in the catalogue would be invisible."* A designer retuning `subdivisions` must not silently reprice the tree.

**Decision (intake Q1 = a):** in this item the table carries **only the four shipped rows** (`spread` starter, `wave_laser` 120/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `cluster` 160/1). All eleven newly derived weapons ship **grant-only**; their price ladder is deferred to AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — Hangar weapon entries are derived from the runtime `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` instead of being hand-authored. Adding a row to `src/data/weapons.csv` yields a hangar weapon entry with no code change.
- **AC2** — Every shipped weapon id except the documented exclusion list has exactly one entry in `HANGAR_CATALOGUE`. Exclusions are explicit, documented data, and must include `cannon` (the always-mounted permanent default weapon, which must never be sellable). Count assertion: 16 CSV weapons − exclusions → expected entry count.
- **AC3** — An authored `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` side table promotes derived entries to purchasable; absent ⇒ grant-only. In this item the table carries **only the four shipped rows** (intake Q1 = a) and the shipped prices are preserved byte-for-byte: `wave_laser` 120 minerals / 1 core, `ricochet` 90 / 2, `cluster` 160 / 1; `spread` keeps `starter: true`. All eleven newly derived weapons (`dual`, `rapid`, `options`, `nova`, `mortar`, `arc`, `rear_guard`, `broadside`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug`) are **grant-only** — `minRing: GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`, zero price, `isPurchasableEntry` false. Hulls, modifiers and power-ups are unchanged.
- **AC4** — The five hex-granted weapons (`rapid`, `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova`) resolve to a real catalogue entry, so they appear as named owned rows in `buildHangarUnlockRows`, are offered by `buildHangarWeaponOptions` and survive `resolveActiveLoadout`. An existing save that already holds these ids lights up with **no migration** (no save-schema change).
- **AC5** — Fail-closed guards run at catalogue build time, mirroring `applyWeaponCatalogueGuards` (`src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts`): non-empty, actionable diagnostics rather than silent skipping. Five guards:
  - (a) full coverage — every `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` id bar documented exclusions has an entry;
  - (b) no duplicate entry ids across authored + derived;
  - (c) every `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` key is a shipped, non-excluded weapon id (catches stale/typo'd rows);
  - (d) every entry's `weaponId` resolves in `WEAPON_CATALOGUE`;
  - (e) every authored `hexRingDefinitions.grants` id resolves to a catalogue entry, or is on a short documented effect-free allowlist. **(e) is the guard that was missing; `rapid` fails it today.**
- **AC6** — Retuning any CSV weapon field changes no `price`, no `minRing` and no other catalogue entry's economy values (pinned by a test that mutates a weapon's tuning and asserts the derived economy is untouched).
- **AC7** — Red-first tests: the coverage/guard specs fail before the derivation lands and pass after. `captureCycle.test.ts:114` flips from *protecting* the catalogue-unknown fallback to *asserting no authored grant reaches it* (the `resolveHexGrant` fallback stays as defence-in-depth).
- **AC8** — End-to-end verification: a harness/capture of a `hex-r1-3` capture shows `rapid` owned **and** rendered in the hangar unlock list and weapon selector. `src/test/hangarWarWinHarness.ts` / the existing capture tooling is the vehicle.
- **AC9** — Hangar UI copes with the grew tree (12 → ~23 unlock rows): the list scrolls and every row stays reachable in `HangarScene` and the read-only `GymHangar`. No regression in the shipped screen-model tests.
- **AC10** — Gym↔game parity (AGENTS.md) holds: the change is data/economy only, no gameplay behaviour change; `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` needs no new divergence row, or one is recorded with its reason.
- **AC11** — Docs updated: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` header (derivation + leaf-import note), `docs/EVALUATION.md` ≈:399 ("a grant the catalogue does not itemise … is owned but contributes no run stats"), and the "three unlockable starting weapons" tree-size statement in `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` ≈:556.
- **AC12** — No import cycle: `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` becomes a runtime consumer of `src/utils/weapons.ts`; the graph `data/hangarCatalogue → utils/weapons → core/csv → configDefaults`/`utils/beat` must stay acyclic (verified, and documented in the module header).
- **AC13** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC14** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Key Files
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — derivation, `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY`, exclusion list, guards
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts` — AC2/AC3/AC5/AC6 specs
- `src/utils/weapons.ts`, `src/utils/weaponCatalogue.ts` — the guard pattern to mirror; `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` source
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts` (+ `.test.ts` ≈:114) — AC4/AC7, grant → entry resolution
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts` (`ownedEntriesOf` ≈:1235) — AC4 loadout survival
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts` (`buildHangarUnlockRows` `:935`, `buildHangarWeaponOptions` `:1017`) — AC4/AC9
- `src/scenes/HangarScene.ts`, `src/scenes/gym/GymHangar.ts` — AC9/AC10
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` (+ its tests) — AC5(e)

## Constraints
- No new model fields on `HangarEntry`: grant-only is expressed with the existing `GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING` sentinel and `isPurchasableEntry`, exactly as `hull-4` already does.
- No duplicate definition of a weapon: an entry **points at** a shipped weapon id, never copies offsets/fire-rate/VFX (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity, `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`).
- Power-ups and hulls have no CSV home and stay authored; this item is weapons-only.
- No save-schema change; `unlockedWeapons` already carries the uncatalogued ids.

## Risky assumptions
- ~~Pricing the promoted weapons is a producer decision.~~ **Settled at intake (Q1 = a):** this item promotes nothing — all eleven derived weapons ship grant-only (`minRing: GRANT_ONLY_MIN_RING`, zero price) and the price ladder is **AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J**. Calibration anchors recorded there: `hardened_plating` 80/1, `ricochet` 90/2, `anti_maw_plating` 110/2, `wave_laser` 120/1, `bomb` 130/1, `cluster` 160/1, `magnet` 200/2, `hull-2` 220/3, `hull-3` 320/4.
- ~~Option B switches on all three weapon evolutions.~~ **Settled at intake (Q2 = file separately):** this item adds no purchase path for `arc`, `mortar` or `options`, so Chain Ricochet, Cluster Barrage and Fan Escort stay unreachable here; switching them on is **AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J**. **Residual risk to pin:** `arc` *is* obtainable through the `hex-r2-1` grant, so a player who captures it can reach Chain Ricochet's owned tier once both halves are live at level ≥ `OWNED_EVOLUTION_MIN_LEVEL` (2) — assert the fusion behaves as designed (`resolveWeaponEvolution`), does not crash the loadout path and does not breach the 6-slot cap or the auto-loadout variety rule.
- **No aggression-budget inflation expected**: `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0` (`hangarEconomy.ts:1470`), so more equipable weapons do not raise `resolvePlayerStrength` / `ringAggressionBudget`. To be asserted, not assumed.
- **Six derived weapons have no source.** `options`, `mortar`, `rear_guard`, `railgun`, `shard_swarm`, `heavy_slug` are granted by no hex, so under grant-only they are catalogue-complete but unobtainable — harmless (the `hull-4` posture) and only reachable if promoted by the price table.
- A `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` id added by a CSV row whose guard rejects it (broken row → code-default fallback) must not produce a *second* entry; the derivation reads the guarded runtime catalogue, not the raw parse.

## Out of scope
- The three uncatalogued **modifier** grants (`armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up` from `hex-r2-8/9/10`). Same class of drift, different fix (either catalogue entries or `GRANT_ALIASES` re-points) — to be filed separately.
- Extending derivation to `POWER_UP_CATALOGUE`.
- Any rebalance of existing weapons, hulls or the aggression model.

## Impact
Players who capture a hex now actually get the weapon they were promised: it shows up in the hangar, can be equipped, and is flown in the next sortie — instead of being silently swallowed by a save field nothing can read.
## Related work (manual)
- **AH-0MWWARFUK009KQM7** — *Bug: Hex-awarded weapons are granted but never appear in the hangar* (critical, blocked by this item): the field-visible defect this feature fixes; closes when this lands and AC4/AC8 are verified in-game.
- **AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV** — *Bug: Ring-2 modifier grants have no hangar catalogue entry* (high, open): the same class of drift for `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up`; deliberately out of scope here, and it removes those ids from this item's AC5(e) allowlist.
- **AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J** — *Feature: Price ladder for the derived hangar weapons and the evolution halves* (medium, created at intake from Q1/Q2): owns the price/ring ladder, the six sourceless ids and the decision to switch on Chain Ricochet / Cluster Barrage / Fan Escort. **Scope creep must be recorded there, not here.**
- **AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6** — *Hangar economy and unlock tree* (completed): the pure rules (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`) this change must not alter.
- **AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI** — *Load the weapon catalogue from CSV* (completed): the runtime `WEAPON_CATALOGUE` + guarded code fallback this derivation reads.
- Related docs: `docs/EVALUATION.md` (≈:399), `docs/OUTER_LOOP_CANDIDATES.md` (≈:556, "three unlockable starting weapons"), `docs/GYM_PARITY.md`, `docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md` §5.1 (parity convention).

## Decisions settled at intake
- **Q1 — economy scope: (a) grant-only for all eleven derived weapons.** `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` carries only the four shipped rows; the five hex-granted ids become ownable, visible and equippable through their grants; the six sourceless ids stay catalogue-complete but unobtainable (the `hull-4` posture). Rationale: the minimal, reversible fix for AH-0MWWARFUK009KQM7, with no invented prices and no new gameplay. Producer answer, interactive reply, 2026-11-25.
- **Q2 — switching on the three dead weapon evolutions: file separately.** Filed as **AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J** — "Feature: Price ladder for the derived hangar weapons and the evolution halves". Producer answer, interactive reply, 2026-11-25.
- **Routine, agent-resolved (no producer input):** hangar copy reuses each CSV row's `name`/`description` verbatim (zero-drift, per the agreed design); hulls, modifiers and power-ups stay authored; the three uncatalogued modifier grants stay on the AC5(e) effect-free allowlist and are owned by AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers
- **Q1 — "Which of the 11 newly-derived weapons are sellable (`WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` rows)?"** Options: (a) grant-only for all 11; (b) promote only the 5 hex-granted ids (`rapid`, `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova`); (c) promote all 11. **Recommended:** (a) — minimal reversible fix, no invented prices, no new gameplay.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-25): "1. A"** — grant-only for all eleven derived weapons. Recorded in the intake-round-1 comment on this item and in AC3.
- **Q2 — "If (b)/(c): is switching on the dead evolution pairs in scope here?"** (Today `ricochet`+`arc` → Chain Ricochet, `cluster`+`mortar` → Cluster Barrage and `spread`+`options` → Fan Escort are unreachable because `arc`/`mortar`/`options` cannot be owned.) **Recommended:** no — a new fusion pathway should not ride along with a referential-integrity fix.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply 2026-11-25): "2. file separately"** → created **AH-0MWWGFDE1001FW4J** (discovered-from this item) with the calibration anchors and the evolution decision.
- **R1 (routine, research) — "Does the brief's factual basis hold?"** Answer (agent, repo research): 16 weapons in `src/data/weapons.csv`; `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` = 12 entries (4 hulls, 4 weapons, 2 modifiers, 2 power-ups) → derivation yields 15 derived weapon entries (16 − `cannon`) ⇒ 23 rows, matching AC9's "12 → ~23"; hex grants are `rapid`, `ricochet`, `waveLaser`→`wave_laser` (alias), `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova` plus non-weapon `extra-life`, `hull-2/3/4`, `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up`; `STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:1470`), so the aggression-budget assumption holds. Evidence: `src/data/weapons.csv`, `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts`, `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/grantAliases.ts`, `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts`.
- **R2 (routine, research) — "Is the drift real, i.e. does anything today display `rapid`?"** Answer (agent, repo research): no — `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts:935`) iterates the catalogue and `findHangarEntry('rapid')` returns `null`. Captured as a defect in **AH-0MWWARFUK009KQM7** (blocked by this item).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **AH-0MW0Q1EYJ007RRFI** – Load the weapon catalogue from CSV (runtime source of truth + code fallback) (completed)
- **AH-0MVZJ6V1J001DA9D** – Hangar War deployments start with no extra weapons in the loadout (default weapon only) (completed)
- **AH-0MUGQBN5T009U4YG** – Refactor weapon fire rates as beat subdivisions and add catalogue-wide invariant (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/Game Design Document.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac10, ac2, ac3 (+398 more)
- `README.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac11, ac2, ac3 (+374 more)
- `docs/BALANCING.md` — matched: absent, ac1, ac10, ac2, ac3 (+330 more)

## Plan: feature decomposition (plan skill, this session)

Seven child items, in dependency order. Test/verification first, then the vertical slices; each is an end-to-end increment (data + pure rules + scene surface + specs + docs note), not a horizontal layer.

| # | Feature | Type | Est. | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Red-first specs for hangar catalogue coverage and guards | task | S / Low | — |
| 2 | Derive hangar weapon entries from the runtime weapon catalogue | feature | M / Medium | 1 |
| 3 | Authored `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` with grant-only default | feature | S / Low | 2 |
| 4 | Hex-granted weapons resolve, display and deploy | feature | M / Medium | 3 |
| 5 | Scroll the hangar unlock tree to fit the derived roster | feature | M / Medium | 2 |
| 6 | End-to-end capture verification for `hex-r1-3` | task | S / Low | 4, 5 |
| 7 | Docs, parity record and full-suite green | task | S / Low | 5, 6 |

### AC traceability (parent AC → covering item)

| Parent AC | Covered by |
|---|---|
| AC1 derivation from runtime catalogue | 2 |
| AC2 coverage + documented exclusions, count assertion | 1, 2 |
| AC3 `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY`, shipped prices preserved, rest grant-only | 3 |
| AC4 grants resolve → visible row, selector option, loadout survival, no migration | 4, 6 |
| AC5 fail-closed guards (a)–(e) | 1, 2, 3, 4 |
| AC6 retuning never reprices | 1, 3, 6 |
| AC7 red-first, `captureCycle.test.ts:114` flipped | 1, 2, 4 |
| AC8 end-to-end `hex-r1-3` capture verification | 6 |
| AC9 23-row tree scrolls, every row reachable | 5 |
| AC10 gym↔game parity recorded | 5, 7 |
| AC11 docs corrected | 7 |
| AC12 no import cycle | 2 |
| AC13 all related documentation updated | 7 |
| AC14 full suite green | 7 |

### Phasing rationale

Each phase is a vertical slice: item 2 lands derivation **plus** its guards, its specs and a module-header note for the import direction; item 3 lands the economy table with the prices it must not change; item 4 lands the capture → row → loadout journey with both integrity directions guarded; item 5 lands the presentation work that the larger tree forces, in the game and the gym. Items 6 and 7 verify the whole path from the player's side.

**Between phases:** re-read the next item's description against what actually landed and update it (in particular item 5's layout assumptions and item 7's doc line numbers) before starting it.

### Implementation notes recorded for the implementer

- **Guard (e) placement (AC5, AC12).** Keep guards (a)–(d) in `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` beside the derivation. Guard (e) needs the authored ring data; `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` has only a type-only import, so a runtime edge `hangarCatalogue → hexRingDefinitions` stays acyclic. Implement (e) so the grant list is an **injectable parameter** (defaulting to `HEX_RING_DEFINITIONS`) — that keeps the guard unit-testable with a drifting fixture and leaves the import direction free to move if the graph check objects.
- **Economy row shape.** `spread` must stay `starter: true` and free, so the side table's row is `{ price, minRing, starter? }`, not price/minRing alone.
- **Exclusion list.** In this item it is `['cannon']` (the always-mounted permanent default, never sellable) — 16 − 1 = 15 derived weapon entries, so the tree goes 12 → 23 rows. Any future exclusion must be added to that exported, documented list with a reason.
- **Re-baselining.** `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` (the "fits the worst-case full catalogue" pin), `src/ai/hangarWarTraversal.test.ts` and the auto-loadout suites are the likely churn points once owned granted weapons become catalogue-known; re-baseline deliberately and list each one on item 5.

## Plan: changelog

- 2026-11-25 — plan run (downtime dispatch): created 7 child items (1 test/verification, 5 features, 1 task), wired 8 dependency edges, recorded AC traceability, implementation notes and the Appendix below. No parent AC changed.

## Appendix (plan round)

Plan-round entries only; the intake-round Q1/Q2 appendix above stays authoritative for the settled producer decisions.

- **R3 (routine, research) — "Does the derived tree actually overflow the hangar screen, i.e. is AC9 real work?"** Answer (agent, repo research): yes. `HANGAR_UNLOCK_ROW_START_Y = 210`, `HANGAR_ROW_STEP = 16` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts`), `GAME_HEIGHT = 540`, and the fixed bottom block's top slot is `HANGAR_BUILDOUT_ROW_Y = 422` (`GAME_HEIGHT - 118`). 23 rows end at y = 562 — 140 px past the block — and `src/scenes/HangarScene.test.ts` currently pins `hangarLowestRowY(model) < HANGAR_RESTART_ROW_Y` for the full catalogue. AC9 therefore mandates real scroll/navigation work, which is child item 5.
- **R4 (routine, research) — "Can guard (e) live in `hangarCatalogue.ts` without breaking AC12?"** Answer (agent, repo research): yes at runtime. `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` imports only `import type { HexRingDefinition } from '../core/hangarWar/hexRing'`, which is erased, so `hangarCatalogue → hexRingDefinitions` adds no runtime edge back to `hangarEconomy → hangarCatalogue`. # Bug: Hex-awarded weapons are granted but never appear in the hangar

## Problem statement

Capturing a weapon hex records the weapon id in `hangar.unlockedWeapons`, but the hangar, the weapon selector and the loadout path all filter against `HANGAR_CATALOGUE`, which hand-authors only four weapons — so five authored hex grants are silently swallowed by a save field nothing can read. A player who wins a weapon hex is promised a weapon and receives nothing.

## Users

- **Player on a Hangar War campaign** — captures a weapon hex (e.g. ring 1's `hex-r1-3`, boss `iron-crusher`) and expects the promised weapon to appear, be equippable, and fire in the next sortie.
- **Player resuming an existing campaign** — already holds the ids in their save; expects them to light up on load without re-capturing anything.
- **Designer / maintainer** — authors `grants:` ids in ring data and expects a referential-integrity guard to catch a grant the catalogue does not itemise, instead of discovering it as a silent player-facing loss.

Example user stories:

- As a player, after capturing `hex-r1-3` I want a named **Rapid** row in my hangar marked owned, so that the reward I was promised is visibly mine.
- As a player, I want to toggle **Rapid** in the weapon selector and have my next sortie start with it firing, so that the reward changes how I play.
- As a maintainer, I want a failing guard when an authored grant has no catalogue entry, so that this class of silent loss cannot ship again.

## Existing state (verified at intake)

The grant path itself works; the presentation and loadout paths cannot see the result. Verified in-tree at intake:

- `resolveHexGrant` (`src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:255-318`) resolves a grant by (1) the alias table, (2) a catalogue entry, then (3) falls back to `isShippedWeapon(id)` and records `{ entryId: id, kind: 'weapon', weaponId: id }` for any shipped weapon id.
- `GRANT_ALIASES` (`src/core/hangarWar/grantAliases.ts:34-46`) covers exactly two authored spellings: `waveLaser` → `wave_laser` and `extra-life` → `hardened_plating`. Both are itemised, so spelling is not part of this defect.
- `HANGAR_CATALOGUE` (`src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts:243`) itemises weapon ids `spread`, `wave_laser`, `ricochet`, `cluster` only.
- `buildHangarUnlockRows` (`src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts:934`) iterates the catalogue ⇒ no row exists for a fallback-granted id.
- `buildHangarWeaponOptions` (`:1004`) iterates `unlockedWeapons` but `findHangarEntry('rapid')` is `null` ⇒ `continue`, so no loadout slot.
- `ownedEntriesOf` (`src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:1235`) drops catalogue-unknown ids ⇒ would not deploy even if equipped.
- `captureCycle.test.ts:114` ("keeps a shipped weapon/upgrade hull that the catalogue does not itemise") asserts the fallback for `rapid` and `core-bank`, i.e. it currently *protects* the misuse rather than forbidding it.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md:399-401` states a catalogue-unitemised grant "is owned but contributes no run stats — the same 'recorded but effect-free' rule the capture cycle uses", which is presented as intended behaviour.

Definitive un-itemised authored grants (computed by resolving all 14 unique `hexRingDefinitions.grants` values through the alias table and `HANGAR_CATALOGUE`):

| Grant | Hex(es) | Kind | Itemised? |
|---|---|---|---|
| `rapid` | `hex-r1-3`, `hex-r2-4` | weapon | **no** — this item |
| `arc` | `hex-r2-1` | weapon | **no** — this item |
| `broadside` | `hex-r2-2` | weapon | **no** — this item |
| `dual` | `hex-r2-5` | weapon | **no** — this item |
| `nova` | `hex-r2-12` | weapon | **no** — this item |
| `armour-plating` | `hex-r2-8` | modifier | no — sibling AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV |
| `systems-upgrade` | `hex-r2-9` | modifier | no — sibling AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV |
| `firepower-up` | `hex-r2-10` | modifier | no — sibling AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV |
| `waveLaser`, `extra-life` | — | alias | yes (via `GRANT_ALIASES`) |
| `hull-2`, `hull-3`, `hull-4`, `ricochet` | — | hull/weapon | yes |

All five weapons are genuine, fireable shipped `WeaponId`s (`src/utils/weapons.ts:97-116`) with real timing data (`:258-280`), so the grants are legitimate design intent and the fix is to itemise them, not to strip the reward. (`core-bank`, asserted in `captureCycle.test.ts`, is **not** an authored `hexRingDefinitions` grant — it is only a hypothetical fallback example.)

## Desired change

Make the five weapon grants usable end-to-end, and stop the docs and tests from describing the swallowed reward as intended.

**Scope split with the blocker.** The catalogue derivation is **not** built here. `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` (Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon entries from weapons.csv, `intake_complete`, producer-agreed Option B) authors the derivation, the `WEAPON_UNLOCK_ECONOMY` side table, the fail-closed guard set — including guard (e) "every authored `hexRingDefinitions.grants` id resolves to a catalogue entry, or is on a short documented effect-free allowlist" — and the red-first flip of `captureCycle.test.ts:114`. **This item is the player-facing acceptance of that work plus the documentation correction:** it verifies the outcome hex by hex, proves the existing-save path, witnesses the guard failing before and passing after, asserts no balance drift, and fixes the statements that currently claim the loss is by design.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After capturing `hex-r1-3`, the hangar unlock list shows a named `Rapid` weapon row in an owned state (not gated, not "unavailable").
- **AC2** — `rapid` is offered by the weapon selector, is toggleable, and the next sortie starts with the `rapid` weapon active and firing — verified through the hangar-war harness (`src/test/hangarWarWinHarness.ts`) or in-game, **not** by inspecting the save alone.
- **AC3** — All five affected grants behave as in AC1/AC2 from their own hexes: `rapid` (`hex-r1-3`, `hex-r2-4`), `arc` (`hex-r2-1`), `broadside` (`hex-r2-2`), `dual` (`hex-r2-5`), `nova` (`hex-r2-12`).
- **AC4** — An existing save that already holds any of those ids shows them owned on load with **no re-capture, no save migration and no schema change** (`unlockedWeapons` already carries the ids).
- **AC5** — The referential-integrity guard from `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` is verified to cover these five grants: it fails on the pre-fix tree naming `rapid` (and `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova`), and passes post-fix. Its effect-free allowlist is exactly the three ring-2 modifier grants (`armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up`) and is documented with those ids — `core-bank` must not appear in it, since no authored grant uses that id.
- **AC6** — No balance change beyond making the earned reward usable: existing catalogue prices are unchanged, no new purchase path appears without a separate decision, and `resolvePlayerStrength` / `ringAggressionBudget` behaviour is asserted unchanged (`STARTING_WEAPON_STRENGTH_WEIGHT = 0`).
- **AC7** — The false statement in `docs/EVALUATION.md:399-401` ("A grant the catalogue does not itemise … is owned but contributes no run stats") and the matching `captureCycle.ts` / `captureCycle.test.ts` comments are corrected so no documentation describes a swallowed weapon grant as intended behaviour.
- **AC8** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `README`, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- **AC9** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

Five hex captures across two rings stop being a lie: winning a weapon hex actually puts that weapon in the player's hands.

## Constraints

- No duplicate weapon definition: a catalogue entry points at a shipped weapon id and never copies combat data (AGENTS.md gym↔game parity).
- Do not "fix" this by removing the grant from the ring data — the ring design intends the reward.
- Do not build the catalogue derivation here; it is `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91`'s deliverable. This item consumes and verifies it.
- Ring-2 modifier grants are out of scope; they are `AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts` — the four-weapon hand-authored subset; the blocker derives the rest here. This item asserts the five weapon ids resolve.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:255-318` — the `isShippedWeapon` fallback; no authored grant should reach it once the blocker lands.
- `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.test.ts:114` — the test that currently protects the fallback; must flip to asserting no authored grant reaches it.
- `src/scenes/hangarWar/hangarScreen.ts:934`, `:1004` — `buildHangarUnlockRows` / `buildHangarWeaponOptions`, the two filters that hide the reward.
- `src/core/hangarWar/hangarEconomy.ts:1235` — `ownedEntriesOf`, the loadout filter that would drop a catalogue-unknown id.
- `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts` — the five authored weapon grants in six places: `rapid` at `:106` (`hex-r1-3`) and `:226` (`hex-r2-4`), `arc` at `:179` (`hex-r2-1`), `broadside` at `:197` (`hex-r2-2`), `dual` at `:239` (`hex-r2-5`), `nova` at `:342` (`hex-r2-12`). (`:119` and `:329` are `ricochet`, already itemised.)
- `src/core/hangarWar/grantAliases.ts` — the one alias table; confirms `waveLaser` / `extra-life` are already itemised, so they are not part of this defect.
- `src/data/hangarCatalogue.test.ts`, `src/data/weaponCatalogueParity.test.ts` — existing parity-test precedents; the natural home/shape for the referential-integrity guard.
- `src/test/hangarWarWinHarness.ts` — the capture-to-hangar verification vehicle for AC1-AC4.
- `docs/EVALUATION.md:399-401` — the false "effect-free" statement to correct.
- `src/utils/weapons.ts:97-116`, `:258-280` — the shipped `WeaponId` roster and timing data proving the five gifts are real weapons.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the blocker `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` ships the derivation and guard; this item then verifies and documents rather than reimplements. If the blocker's scope changes, this item's AC5/AC7 must be revisited.
- **Assumption:** `unlockedWeapons` is already correct in existing saves, so AC4 needs no migration. Verified by reading `resolveHexGrant` and `ownedListFor` — the grant writes into `unlockedWeapons` regardless of catalogue membership.
- **Risk (scope creep):** the ring-2 modifier grants are the same class of defect and will tempt a same-change fix. They are `AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV`; link them, do not absorb them.
- **Risk:** a derived-entry count change (12 → ~23 unlock rows) could break hangar screen layout tests. Owned by the blocker's AC9, but surfaced here because the verification pass will hit it.
- **Risk:** verifying "firing in the next sortie" can be under-tested by asserting save state or catalogue lookup only. AC2 forbids that shortcut explicitly.

## Related work

- **Blocks this item:** `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` — Feature: Auto-derive hangar catalogue weapon entries from weapons.csv (`intake_complete`, producer-agreed Option B). Carries the derivation, the economy side table and the fail-closed guard set, including guard (e) that this bug proves was missing.
- **Sibling defect, out of scope here:** `AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV` — Bug: Ring-2 modifier grants have no hangar catalogue entry (`idea`). Covers `armour-plating` (`hex-r2-8`), `systems-upgrade` (`hex-r2-9`), `firepower-up` (`hex-r2-10`) — the three ids that belong on the effect-free allowlist.
- **Existing state today:** `status: blocked`, outbound `depends-on` edge to `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91`.
- Automated related-work report (from `/skill:find-related`) is recorded in the item's description.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No producer questions were raised: the goal, root cause, affected grants, fix approach and constraints were already recorded in the item, and everything else was answerable by repo search. Verification performed at intake, recorded here for audit:

- **Q (self-answered): Are the five affected grants truly absent from `HANGAR_CATALOGUE`, or is a spelling alias covering them?** — Answer: truly absent. `GRANT_ALIASES` covers only `waveLaser` → `wave_laser` and `extra-life` → `hardened_plating`; `rapid`, `arc`, `broadside`, `dual`, `nova` have no alias and no catalogue id. Evidence: `src/core/hangarWar/grantAliases.ts:34-46`, `src/data/hangarCatalogue.ts:243`; computed across all 14 unique authored grants.
- **Q (self-answered): What is the exact contents of the effect-free allowlist referred to by AC5?** — Answer: `armour-plating`, `systems-upgrade`, `firepower-up` (from `hex-r2-8`, `-9`, `-10`) and nothing else. `core-bank` is only a hypothetical in `captureCycle.test.ts` and is not an authored grant. Evidence: `src/data/hexRingDefinitions.ts:290`, `:303`, `:316`; the blocker's own out-of-scope note.
- **Q (self-answered): Are the five grants real, fireable weapons rather than dead ids?** — Answer: yes. All five are shipped `WeaponId`s with timing data. Evidence: `src/utils/weapons.ts:97-116`, `:258-280`.
- **Q (self-answered): Is the existing-save path really migration-free (AC4)?** — Answer: yes. `resolveHexGrant` → `ownedListFor(...'weapon')` writes the id into `unlockedWeapons` irrespective of catalogue membership, so a save already holds correct data; only the readers need to change. Evidence: `src/core/hangarWar/captureCycle.ts:255-329`.
- **Q (self-answered): Does a sibling item already cover the ring-2 modifier grants?** — Answer: yes, `AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV` (Bug: Ring-2 modifier grants have no hangar catalogue entry). Recorded as related work rather than absorbed into scope.
- **Q (self-answered): Is this item a duplicate of the blocker?** — Answer: no. Duplicate check performed against `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` and the completed hangar-economy items; the blocker delivers the catalogue machinery and guards, while this item owns the player-facing hex-by-hex verification, the existing-save proof, the guard's red-before/green-after witness and the documentation correction. Partial overlap on AC5/AC7 was resolved by scoping this item's AC5 to *verification* of the blocker's guard and keeping the `docs/EVALUATION.md` correction here.
## Appendix: planning-session questions & answers (2026-11-25, `/skill:plan`)

Planning added no new acceptance criteria; the intake brief already carried a goal, root cause, the affected-grant table and an implementation sketch. Three further questions were raised during planning and self-answered by repo research (no producer decision needed):

- **Q (self-answered): Does any existing work item already satisfy this item's ACs (duplicate check)?** — Answer: no. `wl search "hangar catalogue"` / `"weapon grant unlocked hangar"` returned the blocker `AH-0MWW6PNA5008NC91` (`open`, `intake_complete`, Large), the sibling modifier defect `AH-0MWWARIW6003F7OV` (`open`) and completed hangar-economy/scene items (`AH-0MVUXC1GQ00366Z6`, `AH-0MWOWO8KG006K0WJ`, `AH-0MWHW4ALS0039JFU`) — none of which assert the hex-by-hex ownership, selector/toggle and firing outcome. No overlap, so no rewrite or close was needed.

# Shared per-bullet time-scale seam

## Goal

*As an agent / gym user, I want the enemy-bullet advance to accept a per-bullet
time scale, so Chrono can slow only the bullets inside its field through one
shared implementation that the game and every gym run identically.*

## Context

- Parent: AH-0MWW5BI5C006WOI3, constraint "**Shared-core discipline** — the
  per-bullet slowed dt belongs in `src/scenes/core/` (an optional per-bullet
  time-scale hook on `advanceWrappingBullets`) and every consumer passes the same
  resolver" and "**Backwards-compatible helper** — the per-bullet scale must be
  optional with today's uniform-dt behaviour as the default".
- Today's call sites: `PlayScene._advanceBullets` (~:5215),
  `GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets` (~:2183), `GymPowerUpsCombat`
  (`_advanceEnemyBullets` ~:690, currently raw `dt`).
- Adjacent, not in scope: **AH-0MWWDJCPS0005UQB — World slow-motion time scale**
  (blocked) must be able to compose its `teleportTimeScale()` multiplicatively
  with this seam; a pure, side-effect-free resolver keeps that possible. Do not
  implement world slow-motion here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `advanceWrappingBullets` accepts an **optional** per-bullet time-scale resolver (e.g. a trailing `resolveScale?: (bullet: T) => number` parameter); omitting it reproduces today's uniform-`dt` behaviour exactly, so every existing caller and test passes unchanged.
- With a resolver supplied, each bullet integrates position, ages `elapsed`, fades and expires on **its own** scaled dt inside a single call — two bullets in one call advance by different distances — so no scene can apply a scale twice.
- The resolver is consulted exactly once per bullet per call, using the bullet's pre-integration position, and the loop introduces no closure, array or object allocation per bullet (satisfied against the `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` budget test).
- Player bullets are untouched: `advancePlayerBullets` keeps its signature and behaviour, and a test asserts a Chrono-style resolver never reaches player bullets.
- The helper remains a **single** definition in `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts`; `CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`'s duplicate-body guard is extended if a new exported resolver helper appears, and it passes.
- The helper's doc comment states this is the one seam every scene uses for enemy-bullet time scaling (and the composition point for future world slow-motion).
- **Parent AC5 closed by this item** — **Gym↔game parity** — the game (`PlayScene._advanceBullets`), the generic formation gym base (`GymFormationScene._advanceEnemyBullets`, inherited by every formation gym) and `GymPowerUpsCombat` (which today applies **no** Chrono scale) all slow bullets through the **single** shared seam in `src/scenes/core/`, with no duplicated scaling logic; the duplicate-body guard (`CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts`) and the gym-parity docs assertion (`gymParityDocs.test.ts`) pass, updated to name the new seam where required, and `docs/GYM_PARITY.md` records the behaviour.

## Minimal implementation

- Add the optional resolver parameter to `advanceWrappingBullets` and use `dt * scale` for ageing, integration, fade and expiry (one scale read per bullet, no allocation).
- Tests first: default path unchanged, per-bullet divergence, once-per-call invocation, ageing/fade coupling, player-bullet exclusion.
- Extend the equivalence guard's symbol list if a new exported helper is introduced.

## Key Files

- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.ts` — the seam (one definition).
- `src/scenes/core/bulletLifecycle.test.ts` — the new behavioural tests.
- `src/scenes/core/CombatScene.equivalence.test.ts` — duplicate-body / shared-symbol guard.

## Dependencies

- Blocked by `Chrono slow — hot-loop budget guard` (the budget this seam must respect).
